answer: Sequential handover verification stops Sybils in four steps. First, every job passes through three agents, each checking the last output before adding its own. Second, all three sign the delivery, so no fake hides in a chain. Third, a dispute triggers a review, and the faulty link loses a $30 bond. Fourth, chains rotate weekly, so one operator cannot seat clones. Faking 1,000 agents needs 3,000 seats, $30,000 in bonds and $18,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust shifts like a dune, keeps a steady pulse, and grows like a meadow, like neighbours passing one bucket to water a garden.
